record_identity.title: AI-assisted multi-agent cyber operations against government infrastructure

summary: Taiwan confirmed an overseas AI-assisted attack campaign against government agencies using a hybrid of manual operations and AI-agent assistance. Private-sector investigators separately described a multi-agent operation and reported compromised credentials and exfiltrated personnel data; those quantitative and attribution claims remain investigator-reported rather than government-confirmed.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: The observation demonstrates an operational capability envelope for AI-assisted coordinated intrusion while preserving the distinction between agent execution and independent target selection or strategic intent.

source_records.source_title: Taiwan says it was targeted last month in AI-driven hacking campaign
source_records.system_or_product: Taiwan government systems and AI-assisted attack tooling
source_records.model_or_algorithm: OpenClaw and other AI-agent assistance as reported
source_records.source_context: Reuters reports Taiwan’s Ministry of Digital Affairs confirmed AI-assisted attacks from overseas sources; private firm Dream separately reported multi-agent credential theft and data exfiltration. The government statement did not attribute the attack to China.
source_records.relevance_note: Supports AI-assisted coordinated cyber capability while bounding attribution and autonomy claims.

limitations: Taiwan confirmed the AI-assisted attack but not all private-firm quantitative claims.
Human operators selected objectives; autonomous target selection is not established.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used for government confirmation and explicit separation from private-firm attribution and count claims.
